facts.text: I will provide English text written for company internal purposes and want it rewritten in a polite and respectful tone for a formal business proposal in Spanish.
I am helping write sections of a formal proposal to the government of Mexico.
I referenced a document section titled "Tabla 4. Requisitos minimos de la Aplicacion, Sistema Operativo" when discussing browser requirements.
I noted that the listed browser versions are extremely outdated and that some versions are over 15 years old.
I specifically mentioned Opera 9 as an example of an outdated browser version released in June 2006.
I stated that the requirement says the software should be "accessible".
I advised against supporting very old browser versions.
I stated that outdated browser versions do not protect against current security vulnerabilities.
I stated that outdated browser versions do not support modern web security protocols such as TLS 1.2.
I stated that the software uses modern web technologies to provide a dynamic and responsive user experience.
I stated that modern web technologies require a modern web browser.
I stated that in other spectrum auction projects, support is limited to the latest versions of common browsers where all functionalities work reliably.
I stated that support can be extended to allow recent versions previous to the latest one if needed.
I suggested changing the browser requirement to support current versions of Microsoft Edge, Mozilla Firefox, Opera, Google Chrome, and Safari.
I referenced a document section titled "3.3 Fechas de eventos relevantes y entrega de la prestación de los Servicios, Modulo II" when discussing the software development timeline.
I stated that the time required for the project phase depends on the auction design chosen.
I stated that the development of use cases/traceability matrix takes 20 working days.
I stated that delivery of the application in a QA environment takes 20 working days.
I stated that additional time may be required if a bespoke auction design or a very complex auction process is chosen.
I suggested allowing flexibility to explicitly extend the development timeline later in the project.
I gave an example milestone name: "Selección de mecanismo de asignación por parte del Instituto".
I stated that comments about the implications of choosing a given auction design recommendation for the development timeline can be given in the report delivered in Modulo I.

I referenced a specific software requirement example on page 9 involving a bidder receiving a text message or a digital file in a "Bandeja de Trabajo" and it appearing as a pop-up requiring an acceptance action (checkbox) to proceed with reading, downloading, and unlocking the application.
I stated that the example describes a general feature of notifying the bidder that a message has been received and ensuring that the message is read.
I stated that there are alternative ways to implement the message notification and reading requirement, which may or may not include a pop-up window.
I stated that the provider may have an alternative workflow designed, built, and tested thoroughly and proven effective in previous auctions.
I stated that forcing the provider to change the workflow will increase implementation cost and introduce an opportunity for software defects.
I suggested allowing tenderers to suggest alternative implementations for software requirements that achieve the same goals when responding to the RFP.
I stated that being very specific about implementation details can favor a vendor who already implemented a feature in a particular way.
I stated that giving vendors more flexibility for implementing software feature details allows for a more fair and competitive process when selecting a vendor.
I stated that giving vendors more flexibility helps protect IFT from perceptions of favoritism.
